import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Calculate the number of dogs per district (KreisLang)
# Assuming each row represents one dog registration, so we count occurrences.
dogs_per_district = df['KreisLang'].value_counts().sort_values(ascending=True)

# Set a clean aesthetic style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))

# Create a horizontal bar plot using seaborn
sns.barplot(
    x=dogs_per_district.values,
    y=dogs_per_district.index,
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add labels and title for clarity
plt.xlabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Zurich District (Kreis)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Distribution of Dog Registrations Across Zurich Districts', fontsize=14, pad=15)

# Add value labels on the bars for exact counts
for index, value in enumerate(dogs_per_district.values):
    plt.text(value + 100, index, f'{value:,}', va='center', ha='left', fontsize=10) # Adjust x-offset for better spacing

# Adjust x-axis limits to accommodate text labels
plt.xlim(0, dogs_per_district.max() * 1.15) # Extend x-axis slightly beyond max value

# Ensure all labels and title fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
